solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Mike holds very large area for marbled work

indicators.note: Mike holding something means the other letters sit inside his word

parts.note: mike is short for microphone, MIC
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A man called Mike keeps a huge area set aside for his marble craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mike' looks like the NATO letter M, but here it is the microphone, MIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorative pictures made from small pieces of marble or glass set into a surface are this kind of artwork.

clue.text: Stratagem to conceal staff work

indicators.note: concealing the staff means it is hidden away, i.e. removed from the longer word

parts.note: a manoeuvre is a clever plan or stratagem
to staff a desk is to man it

explanation.surface: A cunning plan to hide the employees' work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to conceal' tells you to take MAN out of MANOEUVRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loanword names a single creative piece or an artist's whole body of output.

clue.text: Arab drinking haunt in good yard twice in a lively dispute

parts.note: AR is an abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

indicators.note: the pub is placed in the middle of the doubled pair of letters
twice means the good-yard pair is written two times

parts.note: a bar is a place people go to drink

explanation.surface: An Arab drinker in a pub finds himself in a row out in the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arab' is not a horse or a person here, just the dictionary abbreviation AR.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal British phrase means a noisy quarrel or squabbling argument.

clue.text: Chap, Celt that's transported round back of city in route forbidden to drivers

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go round the single letter taken from the city
transported suggests the letters are carried off into a new arrangement
the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A Celtic chap is carried around the outskirts of a city on a road cars may not use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' mixes CHAPCELT and 'round' wraps it around Y, the last letter of 'city'.
explanation.definitionFit: A lane reserved for bicycles is closed to motorists, so it is a route drivers may not use.

clue.text: Lad touring Dutch clubs, maybe, in close-fitting garment

indicators.note: a lad touring a letter goes all round it, enclosing it

parts.note: a lad is a boy
clubs is one example of a suit of playing cards

explanation.surface: A young man on a tour of Dutch nightclubs wears a tight outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like nightspots, but it is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece garment hugging the torso, like a leotard, is this tight-fitting item of clothing.

clue.text: Swollen source of light over American

parts.note: a light bulb gives out light
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
US stands for American, as in United States

explanation.surface: A light source swollen up over an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rounded and bloated in shape, like a bulb, is swollen-looking.

clue.text: Arrange woman's clothing

definitions.meaning: to arrange or set in order, as with a shop window or troops in line
a frock, a garment worn by women

explanation.surface: Instructions to lay out a woman's wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to set things out neatly; the noun is a one-piece frock.

clue.text: Term of endearment for British tycoon

definitions.meaning: an affectionate word like honey or darling
Alan, Lord ... is a British businessman known from TV's The Apprentice

explanation.surface: A pet name for a rich British businessman.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Sugar is a British entrepreneur, host of the UK version of The Apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: Like honey, the sweet substance is used as an affectionate pet name, and is also a tycoon's surname.

clue.text: Dine then having cooked at last

indicators.note: cooking the words changes their state, mixing them into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook finally sits down to eat after preparing the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finally, after everything, just as 'at last' does.

clue.text: Incisive and largely reliable soldier about 50

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: sure means dependable or reliable
GI is an American soldier
CA, short for circa, means about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A dependable soldier aged about fifty is sharp and decisive.
explanation.definitionFit: A precise, cutting operation is figuratively like a surgeon's; incisive literally means cutting.

clue.text: Figure that's important dismissing Welsh

indicators.note: dismissing sends a letter away, so it is removed from the word

parts.note: weighty means serious or important

explanation.surface: A significant person who brushes aside the Welsh.
explanation.definitionFit: A number is a figure, and fourscore is one such number.

clue.text: Singer with note left in service, say

indicators.note: the note and the left go inside the tree

parts.note: the service tree is a European tree, so service is an example of a tree
B is a musical note

explanation.surface: A singer brings a note and leaves it in the church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like a church service, but it is the service tree, a relative of the rowan.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy soprano in a choir sings the highest part and is named for it.

clue.text: Working language among Poles displayed televisually

parts.note: on means working or functioning

indicators.note: the language sits among the two poles, between them

parts.note: S and N are the south and north poles
Cree is a North American indigenous language

explanation.surface: A language project running among Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but it is the poles S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Shown on a television or display rather than in person, as broadcast pictures are.

clue.text: Foreign letter from Chinese island

parts.note: CH is an abbreviation for Chinese; that the word also begins with these letters is a coincidence, as the island supplies the last letter

explanation.surface: A letter in a foreign script arrives from a Chinese island.
explanation.definitionFit: The twenty-second letter of the Greek alphabet is a letter from a foreign script.

clue.text: Being unrestrainedly enthusiastic, adoring ships at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone gushing with love for ships out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking with wild, gushing praise about something is effusive, unrestrained enthusiasm.

clue.text: Round near ground, leave without paying

indicators.note: ground means crushed or milled, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A round of drinks nearly bought, then a sneaky exit from the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrase means to flee, typically from a restaurant or debt, without settling the bill.

clue.text: Shelve recorded music supporting team

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, after the team

parts.note: a side is a sports team
a track is a piece of recorded music

explanation.surface: A sports team's song put on hold.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert a plan away from attention or postpone it, like putting it on a shelf.

clue.text: Stay more presumably around marine that's vacant

indicators.note: the stay-more phrase goes around the marine

parts.note: staying more is the opposite of going more, so 'go less' presumably
RM stands for Royal Marine

explanation.surface: A marine who lingers is assumed to be dim-witted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay more' is the opposite of 'go less', the jokey reasoning 'presumably' flags.
explanation.definitionFit: The British informal word means stupid or lacking sense, with a blank, vacant look.

clue.text: Pass article with company executives and meet disaster?

parts.note: to go by is to pass
the is the definite article
the board is a company's group of directors

explanation.surface: Passing an item before the directors goes badly.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to be abandoned or come to grief, like things falling overboard.

clue.text: Appreciative expression, it's said, in seaman

indicators.note: it's said means the word is heard out loud rather than spelt

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A sailor offers a word of thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the final R is silent, so TA and TAR sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Tar is old slang for a sailor, a sea-going man.

clue.text: Piece on menu represented element to surface?

parts.note: a bit is a piece

indicators.note: represented means presented again in a different form, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A dish from the menu, reworded, rising to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'represented' turns MENU into UMEN; 'on' just places BIT above it in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The tarry substance is a component used for road surfacing, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Views capturing Rhode Island in long-running TV show

indicators.note: capturing means holding the state inside

parts.note: views as a verb means sees
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Viewers catch a long-running TV show set in Rhode Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running programme is broadcast as a sequence of episodes.

clue.text: Music company once given sum of money for expat

parts.note: EMI was a British record company, now absorbed
a grant is a sum of money given

explanation.surface: A former record label's payout for someone living abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: EMI was a major British record label.
explanation.definitionFit: An expatriate has left their native country to live abroad, as one who has moved away.

clue.text: Gadget offering game in theory? The opposite

indicators.note: in reversed by 'The opposite' means the theory is put inside the game
the opposite tells you to swap the roles the words suggest

parts.note: Go is a Japanese board game
an ism is a theory or doctrine

explanation.surface: A gadget that gives you a game based on theory, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'game in theory' would put GO in ISM; 'The opposite' puts ISM in GO.
explanation.definitionFit: A gizmo is an informal word for any clever device or contraption.

clue.text: It receives scrape among team at inspection

indicators.note: among means the letters are found within the run of words

explanation.surface: Someone takes a scraping among the team during inspection.
explanation.definitionFit: A violin by the Cremona family of makers is bowed, and scrape is slang for fiddling.

clue.text: Made looser — or made one with minimal alteration?

indicators.note: minimal alteration means only a single letter is shifted to a new spot

parts.note: joined into one is united

explanation.surface: Loosened, or joined together, with very little change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with minimal alteration' moves the I of UNITED along one place.
explanation.definitionFit: Unknotting something has made it looser, freeing it from its bonds.

clue.text: Body of water studied on visit, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the words are spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: read means studied, and see means visit, giving the phrase read-see

explanation.surface: A sea someone studied while on a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The narrow inlet of the Indian Ocean between Africa and Arabia is a named sea.

clue.text: Top official in drama cast around north

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go around the compass letter
cast means thrown, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A senior official gets a part in a play up north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' mixes INDRAMA and 'around' puts it round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A powerful senior civil servant, originally a high Chinese bureaucrat, is a top official.

clue.text: Old school figure embracing southern and eastern European

indicators.note: embracing means holding the southern letter inside

parts.note: an Old Etonian went to Eton, the English public school

explanation.surface: A former public schoolboy hugs friends from the south and east of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: An Etonian attended Eton College, an elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the Baltic state of Tallinn's country comes from eastern Europe.

clue.text: Jaunty king is beset by joyful cry

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded, so the cry goes round the other letters

parts.note: rah is a cheer
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A jaunty king is surrounded by cheering.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashing and slightly dissolute, worn at a jaunty angle like a tilted hat.
